cards.text: The Sadducees, a group of Jewish leaders, just questioned Jesus about the resurrection, and He silenced them (Matthew 22:23-33). When the Pharisees, another group of religious leaders, hear about it, they gather together. One crew walks off the field quiet, and the next crew is already stretching on the sideline like, “Put me in, coach!”

cards.question: One of the Pharisees steps up to test Jesus with a question. Who is he?

cards.text: The law expert asks Jesus, “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?” Out of the WHOLE Law, pick ONE, and no pressure!

cards.question: Out of the whole Law, which commandment does Jesus call the first and greatest?
Heart, soul and mind. In the greatest commandment, Jesus is talking about loving God with ___ of you.

cards.text: The man asked for ONE commandment, and Jesus says there's a second one like it. That's like asking for one cookie and getting handed TWO, and nobody's complaining!

cards.question: Jesus says the second commandment is like the first one, loving God. What is the second one?

answers.text: Give to your neighbor in need

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says these two commandments, loving God and loving your neighbor, are small next to the rest of the Law.

cards.text: Jesus says, “All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.” Picture that one hook by your front door holding every coat, every bag and every set of keys you own. ONE hook. Doing ALL the work.

While the Pharisees are still gathered, Jesus asks them about the Christ, the Messiah God promised: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?” The guys who came with the questions are now the ones in the hot seat.

cards.question: Jesus asks whose son the Christ is. The Pharisees answer that He is the son of ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus quotes Psalm 110:1, something David, Israel's king, said in the Spirit: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’

cards.question: In the line from David that Jesus quotes, who does Jesus say David is calling “Lord”?
Jesus asks the Pharisees, “So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?” What makes that so hard to answer?

answers.text: David would be calling his own son Lord
David would be calling an enemy his Lord
David would be calling a stranger his Lord

cards.question: True or false: When Jesus asks how the Christ can be David's son, no one is able to answer Him a word.
After Jesus' question about David's Lord, what does no one dare to do from that day on?
